memory_update.text: HLMN should be tracked as a hidden home-improvement supplier because 2025 filings show more than 40% combined revenue exposure to Home Depot and Lowe's, plus a merchandising/category-management role that may not screen as consumer discretionary.

IBP maps the installer-capacity layer of the node, but its repair/remodel exposure appears relatively small versus new construction; later layers should verify whether repair/remodel can become material.

WSO is a reference leader for local HVAC/R distribution density, replacement cycles, vendor-line access, and contractor relationships, but it is not the main underfollowed alpha lane due to size and clearer market recognition.

BLDR remains relevant as a pro-channel building-products and value-added-components universe member, but later work should separate true repair/remodel exposure from broader housing-start cyclicality.

For this node, the most promising chokepoint variables to test are local branch density, pro-contractor relationships, installation labor capacity, exclusive or hard-to-replace vendor lines, shelf/category-management control, and customer concentration with Home Depot/Lowe's.

Avoid overfilling future layers with Home Depot and Lowe's; use them primarily as customer/channel anchors while focusing on suppliers, installers, distributors, and category managers whose consumer exposure is hidden inside industrial or building-products labels.

node: Housing repair/remodel, home-improvement, building-products, installation, and specialty distribution suppliers
summary: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around housing repair/remodel and home-improvement supply-chain exposure. The node appears less about branded consumer demand and more about channel density, contractor access, installation labor, replacement cycles, private-label or category-management relationships, and pro-distribution scale. The reference lane includes Watsco as a clear HVAC/R distribution leader. The underfollowed lane prioritizes Hillman Solutions, Installed Building Products, and Builders FirstSource because they sit inside hardware merchandising, installation, building-products distribution, or pro-channel supply rather than obvious consumer-discretionary screens.
